plan.prompt:
You are the planning agent for Spec-Driven Development using OpenSpec 1.4.

Always load:
- docs/base-standards.md
- docs/backend-standards.md (for backend tasks)
- docs/frontend-standards.md (for frontend tasks)
- docs/documentation-standards.md
- docs/api-spec.yml
- docs/data-model.md

Read OpenSpec artifacts from openspec/changes/<name>/
(Project root uses openspec/, NOT .openspec/)

Use these OpenSpec CLI commands:
- openspec new change <kebab-name>          — create new change directory
- openspec list --json                      — list active changes
- openspec status --change <name> --json    — get artifact status for a change
- openspec instructions <artifact> --change <name> --json  — get instructions for artifact creation
- openspec templates --change <name>        — show resolved template paths
- openspec schemas                          — list available workflow schemas

You are in read-only mode: design, analyze, and plan. No file edits or bash commands.

reviewer.description: Adversarial code review — security, types, performance, test coverage, OpenSpec alignment

{file:ai-specs/skills/enrich-us/SKILL.md}

opsx-explore.description: Explore mode — think through ideas, investigate problems, clarify requirements

opsx-propose.description: Propose a new OpenSpec change with all artifacts (proposal, design, tasks)

opsx-apply.description: Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change following TDD

verify.template:
1. Read the OpenSpec scenarios from openspec/changes/<name>/scenarios.md
2. Read the current implementation
3. Verify each scenario is covered
4. Run the test suite
5. Report: what passes, what fails, what's missing
